content.text:
**PR #99** (`agent/fix-head-source-provenance`, 7 files, +421/−20) — the core change is sound.

The provenance gate (`worktree || snapshot.Header.Commit == ""`) holds in every path the reviewer could construct: no-HEAD repos fall back to disk correctly, worktree snapshots never route to git, tree-only cache keying is safe because `restampCachedSearchSnapshotCommit` runs on every cache-hit return, and the new reader mirrors `openSource` exactly (same `BatchFileReader`, same `ShowFile` escape hatch, same 4 MiB cap that matches `defaultMaxParseBytes`). No other verb was left behind — `explain` reads no source, `search` already handled `--head`.

Verification done: branch checked out in a scratch worktree, binary built, `--head` exercised on synthetic repos (no commits, dirty tree, file deleted in worktree, JSON/bad-format paths); `go vet ./internal/cli`, the new tests, and the full `internal/cli` suite pass.

Four findings, all low severity — the fatal-on-reader-failure one at `internal/cli/callsite.go:91` is the only behavioral one; the rest are a wasted subprocess spawn on the JSON path, missing provenance fields in `ExplainResponse`, and test suites still pointed at the now test-only shims.

Merge it, with one fix first.

**Fix before merge — `internal/cli/callsite.go:91`.** It's the only finding that changes behavior for a user. Degrade a failed `NewBatchFileReader` to a reader that reports "no source" instead of returning the error up through `runDef`/`runNeighbors`/`runImpact`. That matches how the rest of that file already treats unreadable source, and it keeps a `--head` query answering the graph question when git can't spawn. Small, contained change.

**Fold in cheaply if you're touching it anyway — `internal/cli/def.go:176`.** Move the reader open inside the format switch so the JSON path doesn't spawn a `git cat-file` child it never reads. Two-line move; also stops it skewing `index_latency_ms`.

**Follow-up issues, not blockers:**
- `ExplainResponse` provenance fields — real gap, but it's additive schema work with its own test surface, and this PR's scope was the source-reading path. Better as its own change.
- Retargeting the existing suites at the `*FromReader` forms and dropping the shims — worth doing, but it's a mechanical sweep across three large test files that would bury the actual fix in this PR's diff.

Want me to apply the two pre-merge fixes?
Yes, apply the two pre-merge fixes, open new PRs for the other 2 and fix those as well.

21	// on a long dispatch function it points thousands of lines away from the call,

23	// the primary location is now the call itself.
24	//
25	// The call line is recovered from the source rather than from the parser, so
26	// this stays entirely inside the relation-output layer: the caller's body span

62		// Guards are the enclosing block headers in force at the call, outermost

87	// matches snapshot. A committed snapshot must never be annotated with dirty
88	// working-tree source, so --head reads through one command-lifetime git
89	// cat-file process bound to the snapshot's commit. Worktree snapshots, and the

92		ctx context.Context,
93		snapshot sem.ProviderSnapshot,
94		worktree bool,
95	) (lineReader, func() error, error) {
96		if worktree || snapshot.Header.Commit == "" {
97			return newRepoLineReader(snapshot.Header.RepoRoot), nil, nil
98		}
99	
100		batch, err := gitutil.NewBatchFileReader(ctx, snapshot.Header.RepoRoot, snapshot.Header.Commit)
101		if err != nil {
102			return nil, nil, err
103		}
104		batch.SetMaxBytes(callSiteMaxFileBytes)
105	
106		cache := map[string][]string{}
107		read := func(relPath string) ([]string, bool) {
108			if relPath == "" || snapshot.Header.RepoRoot == "" {
109				return nil, false
110			}
111			if lines, ok := cache[relPath]; ok {
112				return lines, lines != nil
113			}
114	
115			var content string
116			var ok bool
117			var readErr error
118			if strings.Contains(relPath, "\n") {
119				// The batch protocol is line based, so a newline-bearing Git path
120				// needs the argv-safe one-shot reader. It still reads the same commit;
121				// failure never falls back to the dirty working tree.
122				content, ok, readErr = gitutil.ShowFile(ctx, snapshot.Header.RepoRoot, snapshot.Header.Commit, relPath)
123				if int64(len(content)) > callSiteMaxFileBytes {
124					ok = false
125				}
126			} else {
127				content, ok, readErr = batch.ReadFile(relPath)
128			}
129			if readErr != nil || !ok || strings.IndexByte(content, 0) >= 0 {
130				cache[relPath] = nil
131				return nil, false
132			}
133	
134			lines := strings.Split(strings.ReplaceAll(content, "\r\n", "\n"), "\n")
135			cache[relPath] = lines
136			return lines, true
137		}
138		return read, batch.Close, nil
139	}

content.text:
All four findings are addressed.

**PR #99** — the two pre-merge fixes are pushed (`9ad5da6`):
- `openSnapshotLineReaderOrDegrade` replaces the fatal open in `def`/`neighbors`/`impact`. A failed `git cat-file --batch` spawn now costs the answer its source windows, not the answer, and warns on stderr. New test builds the reader against a nonexistent repo root to force the failure.
- `def` opens the reader only for `text`/`agent`. Verified with a `git` shim counting spawns on a warm cache: `--format json` went 1 → 0, `text` stays at 1 and still uses it.

**New PRs**, both stacked on `agent/fix-head-source-provenance` (GitHub retargets them to main when #99 merges):
- **#107** — https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/107 — drops the shims. `writeDefBodies` had no callers at all and is deleted; the other three become `*OnDisk` helpers in a `_test.go` file, so no test-only path ships in the binary and each call site names its reader. Adds `TestNeighborsJSONCallSitesFollowSelectedTree`, mutation-checked by forcing the on-disk reader — it fails with `call site at line 8, want the committed line 7`.

`gofmt`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` pass on all three branches.

One judgment call worth flagging: I left `index_latency_ms` measured after the reader open in all three verbs rather than moving it. It slightly overstates index time for the source-quoting formats, but keeping the three verbs consistent seemed better than fixing it in `def` alone. Say the word if you'd rather have it moved everywhere.
